title: Octagonal top-metal spiral inductor with patterned ground shield (sky130 RF/PHY passive)
topology: A planar octagonal (or square) spiral inductor wound in the thickest top routing metal (met5 in sky130), with a patterned ground shield (a slotted ground plane) placed on a lower metal layer beneath the spiral to reduce substrate eddy-current loss, and an underpass on a lower metal layer to bring the inner-turn terminal out without crossing the spiral itself.
spec_class: PHY-class passive component — on-chip inductor for RF matching networks, LC-tank VCOs, and inductive peaking in wireline PHY front ends

pdk_portability.notes: sky130 (open-MPW variant) does not define a characterized inductor PDK primitive/PCell; the inductor is a custom-drawn structure using the standard metal stack (met5 for the spiral, a lower metal such as met1 for the patterned ground shield and underpass), so the physical model must be (re)derived per-technology from stack-up parameters (metal thickness, dielectric height, substrate resistivity) rather than reused from another node. The modeling approach (Yue & Wong) is fully portable since it is expressed in terms of generic metal/oxide/substrate geometry.

sizing_approach: Choose outer diameter, number of turns, and trace width/spacing on the top metal to hit the target inductance from the Yue & Wong physical (pi-model) equations relating series inductance, series resistance (skin-effect-limited at the target frequency), and substrate parasitic capacitance/conductance; iterate trace width against series resistance (wider traces lower R_s but raise self-capacitance and eddy-current loss) and validate peak self-resonant frequency and Q at the target operating frequency using an EM field solver, since compact analytical models are only a first-pass estimate for a slotted-ground-shield structure.
layout_idioms: octagonal (or circular-approximating polygon) winding shape in preference to a square spiral to reduce series resistance and improve Q for a given inductance
patterned (slotted) ground shield on a lower metal layer, with slots oriented radially and broken to block circulating eddy currents while still providing an AC ground reference
symmetric center-tapped differential winding for differential LC-tank applications, halving the required area versus two single-ended inductors of the same total inductance
wide keep-out / exclusion ring around the inductor footprint on all layers to prevent eddy-current loss and coupling into adjacent sensitive analog circuitry

source.citation: C. P. Yue and S. S. Wong, "Physical modeling of spiral inductors on silicon," IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices, vol. 47, no. 3, pp. 560-568, March 2000.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its physical inductor modeling methodology and patterned-ground-shield technique only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is the foundational reference for the pi-model treatment of on-chip spiral inductors and the patterned ground shield used to raise substrate-limited Q, cited throughout subsequent RF-CMOS inductor literature.

notes: sky130 open-MPW shuttles commonly restrict full top-metal (met5) usage or require IP hand-off review for custom inductor structures, so check the specific shuttle's rules before committing area to one. Because there is no vendor-characterized inductor model, budget schedule for EM simulation (e.g. an open-source field solver) to validate the analytical sizing estimate before tapeout.

artifacts.notes: Octagonal met5 winding with a met4 underpass and a met1 patterned ground shield, drawn at sky130 layer/datatype pairs. Check it headlessly with `klt drc examples/kb/sky130-spiral-inductor/spiral.gds --deck sky130` -- it is clean against every met1 rule in that deck. Regenerate with `python3 examples/kb/sky130-spiral-inductor/generate.py`; that script's module docstring documents where the drawn orthogonal comb shield simplifies the radial slotting described in layout_idioms, and why (acute notches where radial fingers meet an octagonal ring trip the width/space checks). The GDS is a geometry-only structure with no vendor inductor model behind it, so it exercises the DRC path, not the sizing estimate.
